messages.subject: Implementing qq (from Lattice) in ggplot2
parts:
In Lattice, you can compare the quantiles of two data sets with

    qq(f~v, data=df)

where v is a vector that concatenates the two data sets, and f is a variable with two values, which distinguish between the two data sets. In other words, df looks like this:

  v    f
  3    1
  8    1
  7    1
  3    2
  2    2
  3    2
  0    2

where 3, 8, and 7 are the values of data set 1, and the other v values are data set 2.

In ggplot2, I would like to support syntax like:

    ggplot(df, aes(v, f)) + stat_qqobs()

So I wrote two functions, StatQQobs (which calls ggproto) and stat_qqobs (which calls layer). These are shown below. They work fine when f is a numeric vector. But when f is a factor, only the first data set is passed in the "data" argument of "compute_group", and StatQQobs fails.

Is there a better way to do this?

Even when this setup works--when f is a numeric vector--there is still no way to set sensible defaults for axis labels. So it seems likely that I need a completely different design.

Here are the functions:

# Calculations for empirical quantile-quantile plot.  x contains data
# values for two samples. y is a factor with two levels, which
# indicate which sample is x value belongs to.
StatQQobs <- ggproto("StatQQobs", Stat,
                        required_aes = c("x","y"),
                        compute_group = function(data, scales) {
                            var <- data$y[!is.na(data$y)]
                            var <- droplevels(as.factor(var))
                            if(length(levels(var)) != 2) {
                                stop("y variable must have 2 levels")
                            }
                            i1 <- var==levels(var)[1]
                            i2 <- var==levels(var)[2]
                            s1 <- sort(data$x[i1])
                            s2 <- sort(data$x[i2])
                            len1 <- length(s1)
                            len2 <- length(s2)
                            if(len1 < len2)
                                s2 <- approx(1:len2, s2, n=len1)$y
                            if(len1 > len2)
                                s1 <- approx(1:len1, s1, n=len2)$y
                            data.frame(x=s1, y=s2)
                        }
                        )

# Compare quantiles of two data vectors
stat_qqobs <- function(mapping = NULL, data = NULL, geom = "point",
                        position = "identity", na.rm = TRUE,
                        show.legend=NA, inherit.aes = TRUE, ...) {
    layer(
          stat=StatQQobs, data=data, mapping=mapping, geom=geom,
          position=position, show.legend=show.legend,
          inherit.aes=inherit.aes,
          params=list(na.rm=na.rm, ...)
          )
}
